We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps forward are:
1. Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling) -> retrosynthesis: break amide to carboxylic acid + amine.
2. Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene). So retrosynthesis: break α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid to aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe to aldehyde + malonic acid). The target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid is part of amide? Actually we have /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is after the double bond: C=C-C(=O)N... So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH). Then later coupling to amine gives amide. So retrosynthesis: step1: amide disconnection to acid + amine (the amine is an aniline? Actually amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So amine is an aniline (aniline). So step1: target -> precursor1: acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and amine (aniline). Step2: the unsaturated acid derived from Doebner: break to aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid. The aromatic aldehyde is the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which is sulfonyl phenyl attached to the unsaturated chain. The aldehyde would be on that phenyl ring? The Doebner modification uses aromatic aldehyde (e.g., p-tolualdehyde) reacting with malonic acid to give p-tolyl-CH=CH-COOH (para-substituted). So our unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N... The phenyl ring is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. The double bond is attached to that phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring has a para substituent of the unsaturated amide chain. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with an aldehyde at that position: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para-aldehyde). So step2: unsaturated acid precursor is aromatic aldehyde (para-aldehyde) + malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine gives sulfonamide. In our target, we have NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl ring (tolyl). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline (the first phenyl ring with amine). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl ring (tolyl) via N-SO2-aryl. The N is attached to the first phenyl ring (with methyl). So forward: amine (the first phenyl ring with NH2) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) to give sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl). The sulfonyl chloride would be derived from the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl). So step3: sulfonamide disconnection.

Thus overall 3 steps:

Step1 (retro): amide bond cleavage -> gives α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) attached to phenyl (the second phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor A: p-aminophenyl (aniline) (c3ccccc3N) and unsaturated acid (p-aryl-CH=CH-COOH with sulfonyl group attached). Actually the unsaturated acid still has sulfonyl attached to phenyl? The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl that bears the unsaturated chain. So the unsaturated acid is: c2ccc(SO2Ar)-CH=CH-COOH? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via N-SO2-aryl. The unsaturated chain is attached to the same phenyl (the second phenyl) via the double bond. So the unsaturated acid is: Ar-SO2-NH-? No, the sulfonamide is between first phenyl (tolyl) and second phenyl (sulfonyl phenyl). Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: tolyl (c1) with N attached to S(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonamide N is attached to tolyl (as an aniline) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So the second phenyl has the unsaturated amide chain attached. So step3: break sulfonamide to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride of second phenyl (ArSO2Cl). So precursor B: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH? Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be ArSO2Cl where Ar is the second phenyl with the unsaturated chain attached? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl, not the chain. The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl as a substituent (Ar-SO2-). The sulfonyl chloride would be ArSO2Cl where Ar is the second phenyl bearing the unsaturated chain? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl via S attached to that phenyl (Ar-SO2-). The N is attached to S. So the sulfonyl chloride would be ArSO2Cl where Ar is the second phenyl (with the unsaturated chain). So after step3, we have sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and p-toluidine.

Step2: The unsaturated chain attached to second phenyl is derived from Doebner: aromatic aldehyde (Ar-CHO) + malonic acid -> Ar-CH=CH-COOH. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be ArSO2Cl where Ar is phenyl with unsaturated acid (Ar-CH=CH-COOH). So we need to break that to aldehyde (Ar-CHO) and malonic acid. So step2: retro Doebner: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid.

Step1: amide formation: unsaturated acid (Ar-CH=CH-COOH) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> amide (Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). So step1: amide bond formation.

Thus final route: target -> step3 (retro sulfonamide) -> p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl). Then step2 (retro Doebner) on sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride contains the unsaturated acid; we need to break that to aldehyde + malonic acid. But the sulfonyl chloride is ArSO2Cl where Ar includes the unsaturated acid. So we need to apply Doebner to the unsaturated acid part, not the sulfonyl chloride. So we need to consider that the sulfonyl chloride is derived from the aromatic aldehyde (Ar-CHO) which after Doebner gives Ar-CH=CH-COOH, then we convert acid to sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride is derived from sulfonylation of the phenyl ring? Wait sulfonyl chloride is typically made from sulfonation of aromatic ring then chlorination. But for retrosynthesis we can assume sulfonyl chloride is a commercially available building block. So step2: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (retro Doebner). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is ArSO2Cl where Ar is the phenyl ring with aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring, not the unsaturated chain. The unsaturated chain is attached to the phenyl ring at para position. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with aldehyde at that position (para-aldehyde). So after Doebner, we get the unsaturated acid attached to that phenyl. Then we can convert acid to sulfonyl chloride? No, the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl via S, not via the unsaturated chain. So the sulfonyl chloride is separate functional group on the phenyl ring (maybe at another position). In the SMILES, the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring at the position where the N attaches (the N is attached to the sulfonyl group). The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl at the position where the N attaches (the sulfonamide). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride substituent (SO2Cl) at that position, and also the unsaturated acid substituent at para position. So the aldehyde precursor would be the phenyl ring with aldehyde at para position and sulfonyl chloride at the other position. So step2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid, keeping sulfonyl chloride unchanged.

Thus we need to propose three reactions: (retro) amide formation, (retro) Doebner, (retro) sulfonamide formation.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type "mol" root target, children reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 which corresponds to amide formation (amide from acid + amine). That template seems to be amide formation with unsaturated acid? It matches our target? The template's forward direction is amide formation? The canonical smarts: C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5] So forward is from acid + amine to amide with double bond. So retro is amide cleavage. Good.

We need a template for Doebner modification. Search for functional groups broken: C-C double bonds formed: aldehyde? Let's search for templates that break C-C double bond and form aldehyde and carboxylic acid? Actually Doebner forms C=C double bond, breaks C-C bond and C-O bond. So we need a template that in forward direction forms C=C double bond from aldehyde + malonic acid. So retro would break C=C to aldehyde + malonic acid. Let's search for functional_groups_broken: ["C-C double bonds"] and functional_groups_formed: ["aldehydes", "carboxylic acid"] but we need correct functional group names: "aldehydes" and "carboxylic acid" not allowed; need "aldehydes" and "aliphatic carboxylic acid" maybe. Let's get available functional groups.
